input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (acceptable term length) and § 8.3 already caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which meets our preferred pricing position and is not flagged. However, the non-renewal notice window is 180 days, well beyond the 60-day fallback and past the 90-day walk-away threshold, so exit is impractical. Redline shortens the window to 30 days and adds a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder to reach the preferred position; 60 days remains an acceptable fallback.

ops.oldText: unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
ops.newText: unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice prior to the end of the then-current term. Vendor will notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before the renewal date.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and added a 60-day renewal reminder, consistent with our position that renewals must be easy to exit; a window beyond 90 days is not something we can accept. If helpful, we can live with 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice to 30 days and add Vendor renewal reminder.
